name: Dulse Point Silent Week (self-practice)
location: Bay of Fundy shore, Nova Scotia
summary: Silent week on the shore for up to 30 experienced practitioners. A host rings the bell for two sits and is available on request. No talks, no meetings, no teaching. CAD 720.
description:
Dulse Point Retreat Centre sits on the Bay of Fundy shore: six former fishing cottages and a hall, with the marsh on one side and the shingle on the other. We hold two silent weeks a year, in May and September, for up to thirty participants with an established practice.

**Host**
Anja Roald has practised in the insight tradition for twenty years and does not teach during this week. She rings the bell for a sit at seven and at six in the hall and sits with whoever comes. There are no talks and no scheduled meetings. A board by the kitchen door takes names and times for anyone who wants to speak with her; most weeks a handful of people use it once. Otherwise she is on the sea wall or in the hall and can be approached.

**Structure**
Nothing is required. The two sits are offered, and most people come to most of them, but if you are on the marsh at seven nobody will fetch you. The rest of the day has no shape: the marsh, the shingle, the cottages, the hall.

**Silence**
Held for the whole week. Meals in the hall, in silence, at set times.

**Physical**
Restful. The shore is flat, the sits are not long, and the sea air does much of the work.

**Prerequisites**
A settled practice and at least one prior residential retreat of five days. The week assumes you can hold silence and unstructured time without anyone guiding you, because nobody will.

**Cost**
CAD 720 shared room, CAD 900 single, all meals included.
practical: Saturday to Saturday, one week in May and one in September. CAD 720 shared, CAD 900 single, all meals. Six cottages, two or three per cottage. Bring boots, rain gear, warm layers, binoculars if you have them; the wind is constant. Nearest airport Halifax; shuttle arranged, 2.5 hours. No cell service at the cottages; some on the sea wall.
